lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-9054 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/rchen
EDUCATION
Harbor State University | B.B.A. in Finance | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Lakeside Golf Club | Caddie | Metro City, USA | Aug 2025 - Present
- Caddied about 5 rounds a week, carrying bags and reading greens for members.
- Helped the pro shop run the weekend junior tournament.
Crescent Bank | Credit Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jul 2020 - Dec 2022
- Underwrote 60 small-business loans worth USD 45M, and none of the approved loans defaulted in their first two years.
- Reviewed 3 years of declined applications; my findings changed two ratio thresholds and raised approvals from 41% to 48% with no rise in early defaults.
- Writes the covenant-monitoring checklist for the portfolio, cutting missed covenant tests from 7 to 1 a year.
- Built a spreading template for borrower financials that cut each credit memo from 6 hours to 3.
Stonebridge Manufacturing | Financial Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jan 2023 - Jun 2025
- Improved close efficiency by 40% by automating reconciliations and intercompany eliminations.
- Modeled the capital plan for 12 plant projects in a shared NPV template, so every request used the same discount rate and payback rules.
- Wrote the variance commentary for the monthly board pack, explaining each line more than 5% off budget.
- Valued the acquisition target by discounting its free cash flow to equity at the company's weighted average cost of capital.
- Reported a 45% group EBITDA margin by adding the EBITDA margins of the three business units.
- Built the rolling 18-month cash-flow forecast for a USD 600M manufacturer, keeping monthly forecast error under 4% and letting treasury pay down USD 40M of revolver debt early.
PROJECTS
Regional Utility Valuation | Independent Project | Excel | Nov 2024 - Present
- Valued a listed regional utility with a 10-year DCF and a comparable-company check, landing within 6% of the market price.
- Tested the valuation's sensitivity: a 1-point change in the discount rate moved the share value from USD 52 to USD 44.
- Shared the model and a two-page note with the university investment club, which used it in its spring pitch.
Student Investment Fund | Analyst, Team of 6 | Excel | Sep 2018 - May 2019
- Supported the FP&A team with financial reporting and analysis.
- Rebuilt the fund's performance report to show returns against its benchmark, which the committee used at every meeting.
- Built an 18-month cash forecast for a USD 600M business, holding error to about 4% and freeing USD 40M to repay debt early.
SKILLS
Tools: Excel
Methods: financial modeling, DCF valuation, forecasting, credit analysis

items.says: The same cash-forecast achievement appears under Stonebridge and the Student Investment Fund.
items.because: The matching scale, error, and debt-repayment result make it unclear which role the work belonged to.

items.says: Experience is not in newest-first order.
items.because: Crescent Bank appears before the more recent Stonebridge role.

items.says: Education should follow Experience.
items.because: Several years of relevant work history provide stronger opening evidence than the degree alone.

items.says: The Lakeside caddie entry should be shortened and placed after the finance roles.
items.because: Leading with an unrelated current role makes the finance narrative less immediate.

items.says: Carrying bags and reading greens do not advance the finance-focused story.
items.because: Those duties do not connect to the finance experience elsewhere on the résumé.

items.says: Junior-tournament support does not advance the finance-focused story.
items.because: The duty does not connect to the finance experience elsewhere on the résumé.

items.says: The underwriting bullet does not identify the analysis behind the lending decisions.
items.because: The loan volume and value show scale but not the credit skill used to assess borrowers.

items.says: The declined-application review does not say what its findings revealed about the thresholds.
items.because: The reader cannot see the credit judgment that prompted the policy change.

items.says: The declined-application review and its result should lead the Crescent Bank bullets.
items.because: Leading with the policy impact would make it easier to notice.

items.says: “My findings” uses a first-person possessive.
The review period is ambiguous.
“Writes” is the wrong tense for a role that ended in December 2022.
items.because: The present tense conflicts with the role dates and later roles.

items.says: The checklist bullet does not say what monitoring control the checklist introduced.
items.because: The reader cannot tell what changed in the monitoring process to reduce missed tests.

items.says: The spreading-template bullet does not specify what the template enabled or standardized.
items.because: The time saving is clear, but the practical improvement built into the template is not.

items.says: “Close efficiency” does not identify what the 40% improvement measures or compares with.
items.because: The percentage could refer to close duration, manual effort, or another measure.

items.says: The explanation of the NPV template’s purpose is longer than needed.
items.because: The clause after “so” takes attention away from the action.

items.says: The board-pack bullet does not say what the commentary helped someone do.
Discounting free cash flow to equity at WACC uses the wrong cash-flow and discount-rate pairing.
items.because: Free cash flow to equity is normally discounted at the cost of equity; WACC applies to free cash flow to the firm.

items.says: The acquisition-valuation bullet gives no valuation output.
items.because: Without an estimate or range, the scale and use of the work remain unclear.

items.says: Adding business-unit EBITDA margins does not calculate group EBITDA margin.
items.because: Group margin is total EBITDA divided by total revenue, accounting for differences in unit revenue.

items.says: The 45% group EBITDA margin has no period or comparison attached.
The cash-forecast outcomes are buried after the forecast description.
items.because: Forecast error and early debt repayment are the bullet’s most concrete results.

items.says: The Stonebridge cash-forecast and close-efficiency results should lead the entry.
items.because: The entry spans several finance responsibilities, and those results give the clearest evidence of impact.

items.says: The sensitivity bullet does not give the starting and ending discount rates.
“Which used it” does not clarify whether the club used the model, the note, or both.
The FP&A bullet does not name the specific report or analysis produced.
items.because: “Supported” and “financial reporting and analysis” give little evidence of a particular finance skill.

items.says: The FP&A acronym may be unclear to readers outside the team.
The FP&A bullet does not say what changed because of the work.
The FP&A bullet gives no evidence of the work’s scale or effectiveness.
The fund-performance report should lead the Student Investment Fund bullets.
items.because: It shows a clearer investment-fund contribution than the broad opening bullet.

items.says: The student-fund bullet wrongly credits the analyst role with an operating-company treasury outcome.
items.because: A fund analyst cannot through that role free company cash or approve a debt repayment.

items.says: The 4% forecast-error figure does not say what the error was measured against.
items.because: The reader cannot tell whether it means forecast-versus-actual variance or another measure.

items.says: The cash-forecast bullet does not say how the forecast was developed.
The Student Investment Fund entry does not present one clear investment-fund story.
items.because: It mixes a performance report, generic FP&A support, and a business cash forecast.
